title: Geoswitch telemetry thresholding and variant graceful-degrade playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a robust region-selection gating mechanism that leverages real-time latency telemetry (p50/p95) and network health indicators (packet loss, tcp retransmits, region availability) to choose a serving region and, when necessary, gracefully fall back to lower-cost or lower-capacity model variants. Current simple thresholding causes flapping during transient spikes and can route traffic to overloaded POPs or incompatible model variants.
goals: Define a telemetry fusion heuristic combining p50/p95 latency and net-health score to rank regions for routing
Implement hysteresis and sample-size-aware thresholds to avoid flapping on short-lived spikes
Provide a deterministic fallback path to compatible model variants (quantized/short-context) with preserved semantics
Ship a canary rollout with observability and automated rollback criteria
acceptance_criteria: Router chooses a primary region deterministically given the same telemetry snapshot
False-positive failovers are <1% of routed traffic during 2-week A/B canary compared to baseline
Fallback to variant preserves caller-prescribed model_family and does not break function-calling contract (validated by integration tests)
Region choice and fallback decisions are logged and visible in Console with per-decision metadata (p50, p95, net_health_score, sample_count, reason)
Automated rollback triggers if customer p99 latency or error-rate increases by >20% in canary cohort
implementation_steps: Design telemetry fusion function: weighted composite score = w1*normalized_p95 + w2*normalized_p50 + w3*(1 - net_health_score) with dynamic weights based on sample_count
Add sample-size floor and confidence interval check: require min 100 requests in last 60s or fallback to conservative routing
Implement hysteresis windows (decay EWMA over 30s, 3-tier state machine: Healthy, Degraded, Unavailable)
Map model compatibility rules for fallback variants (e.g., full->int8->int4; full-ctx->short-ctx) and validate via unit tests
Expose routing decision metadata in request trace/headers and event bus for Console ingestion
Create canary config: 5% of traffic, 24h warmup, 2-week experiment with automated analyzer job
Instrument dashboards and alerts for: increase in routed error-rate, p99 delta, fallback-rate by customer tier
Run load tests across 3 POPs with synthetic latency spikes to validate hysteresis and non-flapping behavior
Roll out to production after sign-off from SRE and PM
telemetry_queries: PromQL (net health): rate(tcp_retransmits_total[60s]) / max(1, rate(tcp_packets_total[60s])) by (region)

SQL (KV): SELECT region, count(*) as samples, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 95) as p95, approx_percentile(latency_ms, 50) as p50 FROM request_spans WHERE ts > now() - interval '60 seconds' GROUP BY region;
testing_plan: Unit tests for fusion function with synthetic distributions (multi-modal latency, sparse samples)
Integration tests validating model-variant compatibility matrix for function-calling and streaming responses
Chaos test: inject 200-500ms network jitter in POP-B and ensure router shifts after hysteresis window
A/B canary: 5% traffic vs control with automated daily report comparing p99/p95/errors/fallback-rate
deploy_plan: Deploy decision logic behind feature flag to 2 control-plane replicas and one router POP in staging
Run synthetic load for 48h and verify no regressions in request success rate
Enable canary 5% in production for 48h warmup, monitor; extend to 2-week experiment if stable
Gradual ramp to 100% with 4-hour step increases and automated rollback on threshold breach
monitoring_and_rollbacks: Primary SLOs: p95 latency, p99 latency, request error rate. Automatic rollback if p99 or error-rate increases >20% vs baseline over 1h
Fallback-rate alert: trigger if >2% of traffic falls back for a GA customer tier without prior configuration
Circuit breaker: if net_health_score < 0.4 for a region for 3 consecutive 60s windows mark as Unavailable
notes: Decision: use combined p95 and net_health_score as primary ranking signal; p50 used for tie-breaker and short-tail sensitivity
Trade-off: heavier weighting on p95 reduces sensitivity to transient p50 spikes but can delay detection of growing tail latency — mitigated with hysteresis
We chose EWMA 30s as decay to balance responsiveness and stability (empirically validated in simtests)
Compatibility matrix stored in repo: routing/fallbacks/compat_matrix.yaml
Follow-up: align weights with Optimize team recommendations for cost-aware routing (see ENG-91210)
